Muhammad Shah and Alauddin Sikander Shah became rulers one after another. The last
Tughluq ruler, Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah remained the ruler for 18 years. It was during
his rule when Taimur invaded and Tughlug Dynasty came to an end.
Activity: Muhammad bin Tughluq was highly educated of allthe preceding
sultans of Delhi. Using online resources, explore what type of education he
had. What did he do for promotion of education?
Invasions of Taimur
Taimur was a Turko-Mongol conqueror who brought most of the Muslim-ruled parts of
Central Asia and India under his control in the 14th century.He was the founder of the
Taimurid empire of Central Asia, ultimately ruling much of Europe and Asia.
The unsettled political conditions in South Asia
encouragedTaimurtoattemptto invade.Hetherefore
sent his grandson Pir Muhammad with a large army to
launchanattackon India.
The attack proved successful and Multan and Uch
were captured.Following this victory,Taimur
gathered an armyof 92000 andmarchedtowards
Turko Mongol Conqueror-Taimur
Delhi, where he was joined by Pir Muhammad.There, they faced Nasir-Ud-Din Tughluq
and his army withnearly1000war elephants.Althoughfrightenedbythe sight of such
them to win the battle. Overall, Taimur's invasions had deep impacts on the
Subcontinent.
Therewas a tremendous loss of lives and property and Dehli was completely ransacked.
The invasion exposed the weaknesses of the Delhi Sultanate. It invited many foreign
invaders to attack various regions of India and plunder its wealth.
